message.content:
Keysight Technologies Inc reported third-quarter results for the period ended 2026-07-31 with revenue of $1.85 billion against $1.35 billion a year earlier and net income of $397 million against $191 million [D1]. Orders of $2.09 billion were up 56% from a year earlier and marked a second consecutive quarter above $2 billion [D1]. Non-GAAP earnings per share were $3.07 against $1.72 a year earlier, and free cash flow was $403 million against $291 million [D1]. The Communications Solutions Group reported revenue of $1.35 billion, up 43%, and the Electronic Industrial Solutions Group reported revenue of $501 million, up 21% [D1]. Management guided fourth-quarter revenue to a range of $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion, a mid-point representing growth of about 37% on a year earlier, and non-GAAP earnings per share of $3.34 to $3.40 on a weighted diluted share count of about 172 million [D1].

The quarter's central claim is that demand tied to AI infrastructure is scaling, with management saying the momentum in commercial communications continued into the second half of the year driven by the rapid scaling of the AI infrastructure ecosystem [D3]. Commercial communications revenue grew 56% and wireline revenue exceeded wireless revenue for the first time in the company's history [D2]. Management said wireline delivered record orders that more than doubled from a year earlier [D3]. The fourth-quarter outlook came in above analyst consensus, with the revenue range of $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion set against expectations of $1.82 billion and adjusted earnings per share of $3.34 to $3.40 set against expectations of about $2.68 [D2]. Management said demand was far exceeding its ability to supply, that the pipeline continued to grow strongly, and that the 6G opportunity is greater than the 5G opportunity [D3]. Sales leadership said it was confident in delivering another record quarter and surpassing $2 billion in orders for a third consecutive quarter [D3].

What the market is arguing over is the conversion of that demand and the durability of the margin, with management saying the supply chain will remain the governor of near-term revenue and that the supply environment is less flexible than a year earlier [D3]. Management said demand is not the limiter and that revenue conversion is likely to be nonlinear over the next few quarters [D4]. Management also said the one-time tariff impacts this year artificially pulled up fiscal 2026 profitability and will not repeat, leaving a high comparison bar [D3]. Operating margin was 33.2%, up 820 basis points year over year and above the long-term target range of 31% to 32% [D3]. Analysts pressed on whether the order level is sustainable and whether supply constraints are limiting guidance, and management's tone was described as more guarded in the question period than in prepared remarks [D3]. Cost synergy realization of 80% to 90% of the $100 million target is expected on a run-rate basis exiting the fiscal year [D3].

The sell side has marked the shares higher, with the mean of 12 short-term price targets at $418.42 indicating a potential upside of 30% from a close of $321.87, a low estimate of $390.00 and a high of $452.00 [D5]. The consensus estimate for the current year rose 11% over 30 days as three estimates moved higher and none moved lower [D5]. The same write-up holds that price targets mislead investors far more often than they guide and are frequently set to drum up interest in a stock [D5]. The shares had gained 8.5% over the four weeks before that close [D5].
